correctness.rationale: Exact recursive decomposition of trivially perfect graphs, exact integer polynomial-set construction and complete coefficient checks give zero failures for all n<=15 and one distinct violation among all connected n=16 polynomials. Nonnegative log-concave interval-support coefficient sequences remain log-concave under convolution, excluding disconnected n=16. Independent graph-level exhaustive checks confirm the recurrence on all labeled graphs n<=5 and the windmill count on all 65536 vertex subsets. The family threshold is a direct algebraic inequality; no finite extrapolation is invoked.

The known formula for clique-joins proves the polynomial of the exhibited witness, but a formula on a subfamily cannot establish an optimal cutoff or uniqueness across all rooted-forest closures.

originality.rationale: The sharp lower bound through 15 vertices and the unique violating polynomial at order 16 quantify the ENTIRE trivially perfect class, not a single special graph. The earlier clique-join formula covers the windmill polynomial but does not imply global minimality or uniqueness among all trivially perfect graphs. Full-text examination of Omar and Rather plus targeted terminology and semantic searches found no earlier statement of this finite classification; residual unindexed-source risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Sharp positive theorem for all members of an important proper hereditary extension of threshold graphs, complete classification of the exceptional 16-vertex coefficient vector, and an exact infinite family transition motivated by recent shape-conjecture work. These are structurally motivated bounds and a complete finite cutoff, not merely a restatement of the known windmill polynomial. The stronger all-order conjecture remains open.
